About Leightons Opticians & Hearing Care

Leightons is a family-owned opticians and hearing care provider established in 1928, operating primarily across southern England. They are known for their premium, personalised service and investment in the latest clinical technology, including advanced OCT scanning and myopia management for children. Leightons holds a reputation for thorough eye examinations that go well beyond the standard NHS sight test.

Leightons Opticians was founded in 1928 by Henry Oscar Leighton in the town of Marlow, Buckinghamshire. From its earliest days, the practice distinguished itself through meticulous attention to patient care and a commitment to investing in the best available clinical equipment. The business remained in the Leighton family for decades, gradually expanding across the Home Counties and southern England while maintaining the personal, community-focused ethos that had defined the original practice.

Throughout the latter half of the twentieth century, Leightons grew steadily, opening new branches in affluent towns across Surrey, Hampshire, Berkshire, and Sussex. The company was an early adopter of new optical technology, introducing computerised eye testing equipment and OCT scanning before many of its competitors. In the 2000s, Leightons expanded its services to include hearing care, recognising the overlap between vision and hearing health in its predominantly older patient demographic. The combined opticians-and-audiologists model allowed patients to manage both aspects of their sensory health in a single appointment.

Today, Leightons operates approximately 35 practices across southern England and remains privately owned and family-run. The company has developed a strong reputation for its "Ultimate Eye Examination" — a comprehensive assessment that includes OCT scanning, visual field testing, digital retinal photography, and a detailed consultation that typically lasts 45 minutes to an hour. Leightons also offers a specialist myopia management service for children, using the latest evidence-based interventions to slow the progression of short-sightedness. The brand positions itself firmly at the premium end of the market, prioritising clinical depth and personalised care over volume and price competition.

Frequently Asked Questions About Leightons

Common questions about eye tests, services, and booking at Leightons Opticians & Hearing Care.

What is the Ultimate Eye Examination at Leightons?

The Ultimate Eye Examination is Leightons' most comprehensive eye health assessment. It goes well beyond a standard sight test, incorporating OCT (Optical Coherence Tomography) scanning, wide-field digital retinal photography, visual field testing, and an extended consultation with your optometrist. The examination typically lasts between 45 minutes and an hour and is designed to detect eye conditions at the earliest possible stage. It is particularly recommended for patients with a family history of eye disease, those over 40, and anyone wanting the most thorough possible check of their eye health.

Does Leightons offer myopia management for children?

Yes, Leightons is one of the leading providers of myopia management for children in the UK. Their programme uses evidence-based treatments to slow the progression of short-sightedness, including MiSight daily contact lenses, Miyosmart spectacle lenses, and orthokeratology (overnight corneal reshaping lenses). The service begins with a detailed assessment of the child's myopia and risk factors, followed by a tailored treatment plan with regular monitoring appointments to track progress.

Where are Leightons branches located?

Leightons operates approximately 35 branches across southern England, concentrated in the Home Counties and along the south coast. You will find Leightons practices in areas including London, Surrey, Hampshire, Berkshire, Sussex, Kent, and Buckinghamshire. They do not currently have branches in the Midlands, the North of England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland.

Is Leightons more expensive than Specsavers or Boots?

Leightons is positioned at the premium end of the market, and their prices are generally higher than mainstream chains like Specsavers, Boots, or ASDA. However, the higher cost reflects longer appointment times, more advanced diagnostic technology, and a greater depth of clinical assessment. Many patients who have switched to Leightons report that the difference in the thoroughness and quality of the examination justifies the additional cost. NHS eye tests are available free to eligible patients, just as at any other optician.

Does Leightons offer hearing aids?

Yes, many Leightons branches provide a full audiology service alongside their optical care. They work with leading hearing aid manufacturers including Phonak, Oticon, Widex, and Signia, offering a range of devices from discreet in-ear models to powerful behind-the-ear aids. Hearing assessments are free, and audiologists will explain all available options, including the differences between NHS-funded and private hearing aids.

Can I get an NHS eye test at Leightons?

Yes, Leightons provides free NHS-funded eye tests for all eligible patients. This includes children under 16, adults over 60, people receiving certain means-tested benefits, and patients with specific medical conditions such as diabetes or glaucoma. If you also want the enhanced tests included in the Ultimate Eye Examination — such as OCT scanning and visual fields — these are available at an additional cost.

How do I book an appointment at Leightons through eyetest.co.uk?

You can search for your nearest Leightons branch by entering your postcode on eyetest.co.uk. The results will show you available appointment types, prices, and time slots. Select the service you want, pick a convenient date and time, enter your details, and confirm the booking. You will receive an email confirmation with all the information you need for your visit.

What frame brands does Leightons stock?

Leightons carries a curated selection of premium and independent frame brands that you are unlikely to find at the larger chain opticians. Their collections typically include brands such as Tom Ford, Lindberg, Mykita, Etnia Barcelona, and Face a Face, alongside more widely available names like Ray-Ban and Oliver Peoples. Each branch has its own carefully chosen selection, so the range may vary between locations.
